newsitem.title: HUNGARY: CSFB rates Egis as "buy" despite results.
newsitem.headline: CSFB rates Egis as "buy" despite results.

text.p: CS First Boston (CSFB) on Tuesday rated the shares of Egis Gyogyszergyar Rt as "buy" despite the fact that the Hungarian pharmaceuticals company released what CSFB called disappointing third quarter results.
Egis reported its January-September pre-tax profits rising to 4.082 billion from 3.825 billion in the same period of 1995.
"We find these figures to be disappointing," CSFB's Budapest-based analyst Spencer Jakab said in a company update.
"Following our 3.6 percent earnings downgrade for 1996 little more than a week ago we find our current forecasts to warrant a further reduction in light of the latest results."

CSFB attributed a significant part of the weakness in earnings in the nine-month period to what Jakab called "cannibalisation" of the market for blood pressure reducer Tensiomin by other inhibitors entering the Hungarian market.
"The two most significant of these would be Richter's Ednyt ans Bristol-Myers Squibb 's own generic captopril."
"Another weak point is that following last year's impressive sales gains in Germany, exports have remained basically flat in real terms," he said.

CSFB also lowered its 1997 and 1998 forecasts for Egis following last week's announcement that ex-factory drug prices will be allowed to rise by nine to 11 percent next year, or five to seven percentage points lower than expected earlier.

However, in view of Egis's recent correction on the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) and on forecasts of a strong 1997 year for the company, the analyst said "we continue to feel that Egis represents value."
On the BSE Egis shares shed 500 forints to close at 8,500.
